verdict: Netflix grew revenue 15% to $9.8B and added 5.1M members, and because costs grew far more slowly than sales, operating income jumped 52% to $2.9B and net income rose 41% to $2.4B.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago; +21% at constant currency

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $3.73 a year ago (both as reported, before the 10-for-1 stock split)

segments.name: United States & Canada
segments.note: The biggest and richest market — revenue up 16% on 10% growth in average paid memberships and 5% higher revenue per member.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: The second-largest region — up 16%, in line with membership growth.

segments.name: Latin America
segments.note: Up 9% as reported and 27% at constant currency — recent price changes and a softer slate cost it a small net member loss in the quarter.

segments.name: Asia-Pacific
segments.note: Mobile-first plans in price-sensitive markets — the fastest-growing region, up 19% on strong local slates in Japan, Korea, Thailand and India.

opex.note: The streaming platform, apps, recommendation systems and the new in-house ad-tech stack.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Advertising Netflix itself and winning subscribers.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $185M on Netflix's debt, plus $22M of interest and other losses — including a $91M currency loss on its euro-denominated debt — a net -$206M below operating profit after whole-$M rounding.
footerNote: Figures are rounded to whole $M; general & administrative is shown as $418M ($417M as reported) and Asia-Pacific revenue as $1,129M ($1,128M in the shareholder letter) so the chart ties exactly to the reported $2,364M of net income. Regional revenues are from the shareholder letter's regional breakdown.
follow100Note: Netflix reports in whole dollars; every line here is rounded to the nearest $M, with two $1M rounding adjustments (noted in the footer) so the chart ties to reported net income.

takeaways.title: Steady member growth, richer members
takeaways.text: Netflix added 5.07M paid memberships to reach 282.7M, and average paid memberships rose 15% YoY — paid sharing and the ads plan kept pulling new households in.

takeaways.title: Profit grew three times faster than revenue
takeaways.text: Operating income rose 52% YoY to $2.9B on revenue growth of 15% — the operating margin reached 30%, seven points better than a year ago, and net income rose 41% to $2.4B.

takeaways.title: Cash rich, and raising the bar
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $2.2B in the quarter, Netflix raised its full-year FCF outlook to $6.0–6.5B, and it bought back $1.7B of stock while net debt fell to $6.8B.

oneTimers: Currency loss: 'interest and other income' includes a $91M foreign-exchange loss, mostly from remeasuring Netflix's euro-denominated debt (net of hedges) — a paper loss below operating income, not a cost of running the service.
